criterion_notes.c1: Examines household and neighborhood access to piped drinking water networks (acceso al servicio de agua potable de red) in informal settlements of the Conurbano Bonaerense (Metropolitan Region of Buenos Aires) from 1983 to 2015.
criterion_notes.c2: Satisfies BOTH the plain wording of Criterion 2 and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading. Under the plain wording, it analyzes institutional, regulatory, and governance arrangements shaping water network expansion across public, private, and re-nationalized regimes. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading, it directly examines: (1) utility ownership and regulatory structure governing service access across three regimes—public OSN (1983-1993), private concessionaire Aguas Argentinas S.A. under ETOSS regulation and concession rules (1993-2006), and state-owned AySA (2006-2015); (2) differentiated institutional/administrative rules and administrative/labor burdens tied to informal land tenure and unlegalized municipal cadastre status, whereby formal neighborhoods receive turnkey utility expansion via municipal public works departments while informal settlements are routed through social development offices and targeted co-production schemes (Pro-agua, Mecanismo Participativo de Gestión, and Agua + Trabajo work cooperatives) requiring residents to organize cooperatives and supply labor; and (3) municipal and administrative discretion/brokerage in selecting neighborhoods and cooperatives and approving technical works.
criterion_notes.c3: Empirical qualitative/multi-method socio-legal and institutional study combining ethnographic fieldwork in the informal settlement Santa María (2011-2015), semi-structured interviews with utility/regulatory/municipal officials, political brokers (punteros), cooperative members, and residents, analysis of primary project/public documents, and descriptive coverage statistics.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports outcomes on piped drinking water network access and connection disparities (78% RMBA coverage vs. 12% formal connections in informal settlements; 99 completed vs. 484 unfinished Agua + Trabajo modules serving an estimated 165,294 people vs. >3.3 million in formal neighborhoods) as well as settlement-level network extension, service interruptions/cutoffs, low pressure, pipe bursts, and water contamination in Santa María.
criterion_notes.c5: Clearly identifies the population and units of analysis (informal settlements in the Conurbano Bonaerense, Argentina, with an ethnographic settlement case study in Santa María and interviews with officials, intermediaries, and residents), exposure (utility ownership regimes and targeted co-production/administrative rules governing informal settlement water network expansion), outcomes (formal vs. alternative piped water connections, network extension, continuity, and pressure), and study design (ethnographic and qualitative multi-method case study).
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Spanish (with Spanish, English, and Portuguese abstracts). Eligible under Criterion 10 because translation from the provided Spanish full text is straightforward/feasible and the study provides directly relevant empirical mechanism evidence on informal settlement water access, utility ownership regimes, and administrative/co-production burdens; log translation method and translator in extraction_note during data extraction.

raw_response.exposure: Utility ownership and regulatory regimes (public OSN 1983-1993, private concessionaire AASA 1993-2006, and re-nationalized public AySA 2006-2015) and differentiated institutional/administrative rules for informal settlements lacking formal land tenure/cadastre legalization—specifically routing through municipal social development departments, municipal discretion in neighborhood/cooperative selection, targeted co-production schemes (Pro-agua, Mecanismo Participativo de Gestión, Agua + Trabajo cooperatives), and reliance on political/community intermediaries—versus turnkey utility provision in formal neighborhoods.
raw_response.outcome: Access to and extension of piped drinking water networks (formal connections vs. alternative co-produced extensions; completed vs. unfinished Agua + Trabajo modules and population served) and service continuity, water pressure, pipe ruptures, and water quality/contamination at the settlement level.
raw_response.population_and_sample: Residents and informal settlements (asentamientos informales) of the Conurbano Bonaerense in the Metropolitan Region of Buenos Aires (RMBA), Argentina (settlement- and household/cooperative-level qualitative case study in the informal settlement Santa María, 2011-2015, plus semi-structured interviews with utility/regulatory/municipal officials, political brokers, cooperative workers, and neighbors).
raw_response.rationale: Include for the systematic review (mechanism synthesis). The paper provides primary empirical evidence (ethnography in Santa María from 2011 to 2015, semi-structured interviews with utility/regulatory officials and local intermediaries/residents, document analysis, and descriptive utility/census data) on piped drinking water access in informal settlements of Greater Buenos Aires (1983-2015). It satisfies both the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading of Criterion 2 by analyzing how utility ownership/regulatory structure (public OSN, private AASA concession, and re-nationalized AySA), unlegalized tenure/cadastre status, discretionary municipal routing (social development vs. public works), and institutionalized co-production programs (Pro-agua, MPG, Agua + Trabajo) impose heavy administrative, organizational, and labor burdens on informal settlement residents and intermediaries compared with turnkey provision in formal neighborhoods, resulting in lower formal connection rates and precarious, interrupted service. Full text is in Spanish (with English and Portuguese abstracts) and translation is feasible per Criterion 10.
raw_response.study_design: Qualitative multi-method case study combining ethnographic fieldwork (2011-2015), semi-structured interviews, document analysis, and descriptive statistics
